terra.problem: The quotation uses the LORD’s first-person words, but the lead-in identifies Moses and Aaron rather than the LORD as the speaker.
The earlier plague of frogs is outside this passage and needs its own reference. The first-person quotation also needs the LORD identified as its speaker.
The text calls them Pharaoh’s officials; it does not say they are the people closest to him.
Saying the officials are done waiting states an inferred feeling as fact.
The text does not say the officials are standing in a room.
The claim that the officials are not speaking because they are Moses’ fans speculates about their reason, even though it is marked as a guess.
Papa Dorin must not call a baker’s answer wrong.
Saying that no green plants made it suggests the plants did not survive. The text says nothing green was left on any tree or plant.
Not a leaf survived goes beyond the text’s statement that nothing green was left on any tree or plant.
The text says Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron, not that he spoke quickly.
The claim that Pharaoh grumbles plenty elsewhere is unsupported and has no reference. The text also says he quickly summoned Moses and Aaron, not that he spoke in a hurry.
Verse 28 has Pharaoh telling Moses to depart; it does not say he sends both Moses and Aaron away.
The locusts were brought by an east wind and carried away by a west wind, not by the same wind.
The reference to Papa Dorin’s experience in the dark does not identify the drawer, so a baker unfamiliar with his backstory has no context.
Calling them two kinds of evening adds a time of day to an account of darkness lasting three days.
Pharaoh says the animals must stay behind; the text does not say he kept or took possession of them.
The passage does not say that Pharaoh’s threat ends the meeting.
Calm as can be states Moses’ manner or feeling as fact, though the text does not give it.
